what: Ferrari makes and sells sports cars in deliberately limited numbers, along with Formula One racing, and licenses its brand. It keeps production below demand so that buyers wait and resale values stay high.
customers: Wealthy individual buyers worldwide, many of them repeat customers given priority for limited editions.
money: sales of new vehicles, personalisation options and parts
Formula One sponsorship and prize money, licensing and merchandise
moat: A brand that cannot be bought or rebuilt, combined with deliberate scarcity: it could sell far more cars than it chooses to build.
risks: Demand depends on the wealth of a small number of buyers
Moving to electric models risks diluting what customers value about the brand
Formula One results affect brand perception
Tariffs on European cars entering the United States raise prices
opportunities: Personalisation options carry very high margins and keep rising per car
Operating margin near 30% is unmatched among carmakers
The order book extends well beyond a year, giving unusual visibility
watch: Shipments with the mix of limited-series cars, and the personalisation share of revenue.
